## VERIFIED and MERGED — Gerrit 1406, commit 2613827564

All five criteria verified by me against the change itself, not on the implementing agent's report.

* **AC1 — readiness requires the FIELDS, not a `serverInfo` 200:** new
  `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py` owns `FIELD_PATH = '/rest/api/2/field'` and
  `REQUIRED_FIELDS = ('Epic Link', 'Epic Name')`, and `await_required_fields` is what the harness now
  waits on.
* **AC2 — bounded budget, self-diagnosing on expiry:** `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S = 600.0`, and
  `not_ready_message` embeds `describe_inventory(...)` so an expiry names the inventory it actually
  observed.
* **AC3 — no longer conflates the two causes:** the module explicitly separates 'not registered yet'
  from 'this image does not offer them at all (a GENUINE DEGRADE)' and tells the reader how to tell
  them apart.
* **AC4 — ONE shared definition, so the paths cannot drift:** both consumers DELEGATE rather than
  duplicate — `conftest.py` imports `jira_dc_field_readiness` and calls `await_required_fields`, and
  `jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py` does the same, its comment stating it 'delegates the whole
  readiness definition'. This is the criterion 1387 broke by fixing only the probe.
* **AC5 — the load-bearing negative assertion now exists**, in three cells:
  `test_a_system_only_field_inventory_reads_as_not_ready`,
  `test_the_not_ready_failure_dumps_the_observed_inventory`, and
  `test_an_unreadable_field_inventory_reads_as_not_ready`.

### Why my earlier 'closure candidate' assessment was WRONG

I twice reported this ticket as nearly done because 'the fix landed in 1387'. Checking the commit
rather than the subject line: **1387 changed exactly ONE file** (`jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py`)
and added NO tests, leaving the harness on `serverInfo` — and so it CREATED the drift AC4 exists to
forbid. Same shape as 1a9f/39c1: diagnosed, partially addressed, easy to mistake for done.

### The root cause was proved by discriminating experiment, not source reading

Stubbing the transport so `serverInfo` answers 200 alongside a system-only inventory:

    RESULT: wait_for_jira_dc_ready RETURNED (declared READY)
    paths polled: ['/rest/api/2/serverInfo']
    missing required fields at the moment it declared ready: ['Epic Link', 'Epic Name']

`paths polled` is the discriminator — it rules out 'checks fields but too leniently' and
'ordering/timing' in one line. The gate was STRUCTURALLY blind.

### A mutation SURVIVED, and that is the good news

Treating an unusable read as ready survived the first mutation pass — a real gap — so
`test_an_unreadable_field_inventory_reads_as_not_ready` was added rather than declaring the matrix
complete. That is the discipline change 1398 taught this epic the hard way: **a mutation check only
tests the axes its fixture varies.**

### Landing note

CI returned `Verified -1` on
`test_concurrency_regression.py::test_plan_review_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union` ('clones do not share
a base') on ubuntu-py3.11 ONLY, while the IDENTICAL patchset passed on the other three matrix legs;
this change touches no plan-review, concurrency, clone or sidecar code. `recheck` (not
`recheck-review`, which would have discarded a clean `LLM-Review +1`) re-ran it green, confirming the
flake rather than assuming it.

Sibling filed: [rebar:4a6d-5bbc-44f4-4a56] — a THIRD live-DC channel (the capability-map workflow)
gates on the same `serverInfo` curl loop and is WORSE, because it reports rather than fails: a run
starting too early would silently record a wrong declared contract.

Accepted residual: `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` is now 916 LOC and the module-size gate
scopes only `src/rebar/**`, so nothing enforces it there. It was 822 before this change.

Closing `--class preexisting`: the weak readiness gate predates this epic's work.
